_README: B1 SPEAKING — six examiner cards, one per page, each with its own AI picture.
Card images live in tools/assets/speaking/ and are generated by
Give each candidate ONE card. Questions are open and natural — no grammar targeting.
The rubric page at the end is shared by all six cards.
title: Speaking Examination
subtitle: Interview · Picture · Topic Talk
warning: EXAMINER COPY — DO NOT SHOW THIS PAPER TO THE CANDIDATE
instructions: Enter the candidate's name, class and number in the boxes above before you begin.
Give the candidate ONE card. Students sitting together should receive different cards.
Run the three parts in order: A Interview, B Describe the picture, C Topic talk.
Show the candidate ONLY the picture in Part B. Do not let them read the questions.
Keep to the timings on the card. Do not exceed 10 minutes per candidate.
Score the four rubric rows from 1 to 5 as the candidate speaks, not afterwards.
information: Part A carries 5 marks, Part B 5 marks and Part C 10 marks.
Allow the candidate ONE minute of preparation before the Part C talk.
Prompt only if the candidate stops for more than 10 seconds.
This result is reported separately from the /100 written paper.

cards.image_prompt: A warm, friendly flat-illustration of a family of four relaxing together in a bright living room — two parents and two young children sitting on a sofa, bookshelf and house plants behind them, big window with soft daylight. Cheerful modern vector style, clean rounded shapes, soft blue and warm orange palette, no text, no words, no letters.
interview: Tell me about your family.
Where do you live, and who do you live with?
What does your family usually do together?
Is your home quiet or busy? Why?
picture: What can you see in this picture?
What are the people doing?
How do you think they feel?
Would you like to spend time in a place like this? Why / why not?
topic_points: What do you usually do together?
What is special about your family?
What do you enjoy doing with them?
cards.followup: What is one thing you would like to do with your family in the future?

cards.image_prompt: A warm, friendly flat-illustration of a busy modern workplace — a small team of four adults around a table with laptops and papers, one person standing and presenting at a whiteboard with simple charts, large windows and city view behind. Cheerful modern vector style, clean rounded shapes, soft blue and warm orange palette, no text, no words, no letters.
interview: What job would you like to do? Why?
Does anyone in your family work? What do they do?
Would you prefer to work indoors or outdoors?
What makes a job a good job?
picture: What can you see in this picture?
What are the people doing?
Do they look happy at work? Why do you think so?
Would you like to work in a place like this? Why / why not?
topic_points: What skills do you need for it?
What would be difficult about it?
cards.followup: Is it better to have a job you love or a job that pays well? Why?

cards.image_prompt: A warm, friendly flat-illustration of travellers at a sunny airport departure gate — a young couple with suitcases and backpacks looking out a huge window at a plane, a family with a trolley nearby, palm trees visible outside. Cheerful modern vector style, clean rounded shapes, soft blue and warm orange palette, no text, no words, no letters, no signage.
interview: Do you like travelling? Why / why not?
Tell me about a place you have visited.
Do you prefer the mountains or the sea?
Who do you usually travel with?
picture: What can you see in this picture?
Where are these people going, do you think?
How do you think they feel?
Do you enjoy airports? Why / why not?
cards.followup: If you could travel anywhere tomorrow, where would you go?

cards.image_prompt: A warm, friendly flat-illustration of friends sharing a meal at a lively restaurant table — four people laughing, plates of colourful food and glasses between them, a waiter arriving with a tray, warm hanging lamps above. Cheerful modern vector style, clean rounded shapes, soft blue and warm orange palette, no text, no words, no letters, no menus with writing.
interview: What is your favourite food?

picture: What can you see in this picture?

Would you like to eat here? Why / why not?
topic_points: Where were you, and who were you with?
